title: borg mount showing the wrong file version?
body:
Versions:
- borg 1.4.0 (debian package, depends on pyfuse3 for FUSE support)
- Debian Trixie
- kernel: Debian 6.12.57-1 (2025-11-05) (with uname -v)
- diverse fuse versions:
```
libfuse2t64/stable,now 2.9.9-9 amd64  [Installiert,automatisch]
libfuse3-4/stable,now 3.17.2-3 amd64  [Installiert,automatisch]
python3-fuse/stable,now 2:1.0.9-1+b1 amd64  [Installiert,automatisch]
python3-pyfuse3/stable,now 3.4.0-3+b3 amd64  [Installiert,automatisch]
```


i will be looking at 2 versions (though really just one, for brevity) of the same borg repo, one version being newer, one i have pulled from a zfs snapshot made on the 30th of november.


The older one looks like this:
```
$borg list <repo path>
1705_16022025                        Sun, 2025-02-16 17:08:41 [05fe4bd41704ba5a594fd5ddec47ab8fa3a6811bbd08e413f53fc9cfb1f667db]
...
shortened for brevity
...
MartinPC-2025-11-29T23:00:02.625868  Sat, 2025-11-29 23:00:02 [915a522e821dfc11a72a0b1c59730dedb4a82d6ac38b4de27a66dab1a75b461d]
```

the newer one like this

```
$borg list <repo path>
1705_16022025                        Sun, 2025-02-16 17:08:41 [05fe4bd41704ba5a594fd5ddec47ab8fa3a6811bbd08e413f53fc9cfb1f667db]
...
shortened for brevity
...
MartinPC-2025-12-20T18:00:02.097987  Sat, 2025-12-20 18:00:02 [b5295694e845c2d32c0e1d4b0f652eae94e04d5688719bca0648767d74582377]
```
The repos contain backups mainly for the last month


these are the files the issue occurs with
```
$ ls -l <loads of path>/*
-rw-rw-r-- 1 martin martin 25603324 28. Dez 12:26 "<loads of path>/HonourMode.lsv"
-rw-rw-r-- 1 martin martin    39240 28. Dez 12:26 "<loads of path>/HonourMode.WebP"
$ sha256sum <loads of path>/*
ab59b0ea708e39c1a1a05ca72eae3a6b73c97d2cd9fdfa90014b445f59b36c67  <loads of path>/HonourMode.lsv
012fdefaff015f53949ae54ea01f3a506ab623c18535f66aafbf81d0da6c9b0f  <loads of path>/HonourMode.WebP
```


As you can see the mtime is the 28th of December (2025) which is when (i presume) the savegame got corrupted. and the shasum is there to verify its not just a time displaying error, these are the 2 files this occurs with


now comes the interesting part:

first mount the borg repo to mp3:
```
borg mount <repo> mp3
```
then examine the files in question:

```
$ for d in mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-*T23*; do echo "Running in $d"; (ls -l $d/<loads of file path>/*; ); doneRunning in mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-07T23:00:02.701843
-rw-rw-r-- 1 martin martin 25603324 28. Dez 12:26 "mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-07T23:00:02.701843<loads of file path>HonourMode.lsv"
-rw-rw-r-- 1 martin martin    39240 28. Dez 12:26 "mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-07T23:00:02.701843<loads of file path>HonourMode.WebP"
...

-rw-rw-r-- 1 martin martin    39240 28. Dez 12:26 "mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-19T23:00:01.614044<loads of file path>HonourMode.WebP"
```

and the sha256sum

```
$ for d in mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-*T23*; do echo "Running in $d"; (sha256sum $d/<loads of file path>/*; ); done
ab59b0ea708e39c1a1a05ca72eae3a6b73c97d2cd9fdfa90014b445f59b36c67  mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-07T23:00:02.701843<loads of file path>HonourMode.lsv

012fdefaff015f53949ae54ea01f3a506ab623c18535f66aafbf81d0da6c9b0f  mp3/MartinPC-2025-12-19T23:00:01.614044<loads of file path>HonourMode.WebP
```
it does the same thing with the older repo, ill ommit it because then the wall of text would become even larger, but i can provide it if necessary

so in short:

borg appears to be showing me a version of this file which is newer than the date the backup was made, even with a repo which itself was pulled from a zfs snapshot made before the file was modified.


this leads me to believe there is a potential bug with the way borg mount shows me files.

Yeah, seems to be a mount issue (standard view).

If you are primarily interested in the versions of some specific files, you could also try the "versions" mount option. That builds the filesystem view a bit differently for that purpose.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This test does **not** reproduce the issue, tested on current 1.4-maint branch (quite similar to 1.4.3 release):
```
    @participant3.skipUnless(llfuse, 'llfuse not installed')
    def test_fuse_standard_view_history(self):
        self.cmd('init', '--encryption=repokey', self.repository_location)
        self.create_regular_file('test', contents=b'first')
        self.cmd('create', self.repository_location + ':<nick>', 'input')
        self.create_regular_file('test', contents=b'second')
        self.cmd('create', self.repository_location + ':<nick>', 'input')
        mountpoint = os.path.join(self.tmpdir, 'mountpoint')
        # mount the whole repository:
        with self.fuse_mount(self.repository_location, mountpoint):
            path1 = os.path.join(mountpoint, 'archive1', 'input', 'test')
            path2 = os.path.join(mountpoint, 'archive2', 'input', 'test')
            assert os.stat(path1).st_mtime_ns < os.stat(path2).st_mtime_ns
            with open(path1, 'rb') as f:
                contents1 = f.read()
            with open(path2, 'rb') as f:
                contents2 = f.read()
            assert contents1 == b'first'
            assert contents2 == b'second'
```

I also ran the test with the 1.4.0 code, no problem either.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I'll check our code in fuse.py whether there is some problem so that files of same path (but from different archives) can be confused with each other (like mapping them to the same inode).

IF there was such a bug, it would only affect the "mount a repo" use case, but likely not:
- the versions view
- mounting a single archive only (not the whole repo)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter If you can reproduce the issue, you could please try whether the fixes from #9246 fix the issue.

As it looks to me now, the bug can only happen if there is an issue and it does not reach the normal end of the archive while building the fuse fs for that archive.

Reproduction could be like:
- reproduce the issue w/o fix
- problem goes away with the fix
- problem comes back when removing the fix

comments.author: participant1

I added the corruption label because what you see in the fuse mount can be corrupted (like showing a wrong file's metadata and data). It does NOT corrupt the repository though.

PR #9246 is trying to fix this, but the root cause is still unclear.

comments.author: participant1

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hmm, I did some more digging and maybe the first analysis was wrong. borg is not async (does not use "await"), not multi-threaded and trio also uses only one thread. So there should be no way that multiple lazy loadings of archives could overlap. The thread lock added in the PR does no harm, but guess is not necessary to fix a bug in the current code.

But then we still miss an explanation about why this issue exists.

Was it the unlikely write_offset problem?

comments.body:
Please double check (they all show the same device and inode, which is unexpected): are these really the stat outputs from the fuse mount vs. the original file in your normal filesystem?

Side note: I checked the 1.4 fuse code whether it accidentally assigns the dev/inode from the archived item:
- 1.4 does not archive st_dev and st_ino
- when asked for the attributes of `inode`, it puts exactly that `inode` into the reply (not something from the archived item)
- inode numbers in the fuse fs are freshly generated when borg loads an archive, from an always increasing offset.
